title: How Can You Be Creative If You Don't Know Who You Are?
description: Choe asks viewers to state who they are, traces adult hardness back to events that closed childhood openness, challenges swings between grandiosity and worthlessness, and uses a stripped-down painting phase to imagine beginning again.
summary: Choe asks viewers to state who they are, traces adult hardness back to events that closed childhood openness, challenges swings between grandiosity and worthlessness, and uses a stripped-down painting phase to imagine beginning again. This is an official-channel creative lesson or reflection, not clinical treatment or a universal formula. Its chronological map follows the route's own transcript and distinguishes art-making instructions from autobiographical claims, jokes and metaphors. Visually dependent technique still requires the source video.
